rule: 1: where a document says a figure increased or declined from A to B, B is current and A belongs to an earlier date, so B is preferred. 2: where the same document states a numerator and denominator (e.g. beds occupied and bed capacity), an occupancy percentage consistent with them (within 0.5 percentage points) is preferred over a printed percentage that contradicts them. 3: otherwise the headline figure block (it reads like a flattened table fragment: newlines, run-together labels) beats a narrative sentence. 4: a row with no conflict is preferred. Checked first whether ambiguous_key was keyed too coarsely: it was, missing country and unit. Without country, a national total for Uganda collided under one key with the national total for the Democratic Republic of the Congo (afro-03, afro-05 to afro-10), and a total collided with its own confirmed/suspected breakdown from one sentence. Keying on country and unit as well resolves 12 of the original 25 conflict groups with no judgement; unit never actually differs within a surviving group. R/lib/capacity_preferred.R implements this.

note: One sentence gives a national total and its confirmed/suspected breakdown: '309 patients were in isolation..., including 116 confirmed and 193 suspected cases' (116+193=309). None of rules 1-3 apply (no change wording, not an occupancy percentage, one shared narrative quote). The total matches what patients_in_isolation at national level is defined to mean; the other two are its own components, not competing readings of the same quantity.

'six suspected and four confirmed cases reportedly absconded from care facilities' gives two case-status sub-counts and no total. Unlike the patients_in_isolation group above, no row states the sum (10), so preferring either 6 or 4 alone would misrepresent the indicator rather than choose between two readings of it. Left unsettled: both rows preferred = FALSE.

33 is 'bed capacity increasing to 1050 across 33 treatment facilities', the same quantity this indicator carries in every other week. 8 is 'IPC/WASH assessments were also completed at all eight Ebola treatment centres (ETCs)': a count of one kind of site in an assessment sentence, keyed alike by the extraction. 33 preferred; 8 kept with preferred = FALSE.
